data.title: Metro Brands Earnings Call Signals Disciplined Growth
data.description:
Metro Brands Ltd. ((IN:METROBRAND)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Metro Brands’ latest earnings call struck a broadly upbeat tone, with management highlighting double-digit growth in revenue, EBITDA and profit, healthier gross margins and solid traction in e-commerce. Executives acknowledged cost and inventory pressures and uneven performance in some newer formats, but stressed disciplined expansion and a medium- to long-term horizon for scaling brands like Clarks, Crocs and FILA.

Strong Q2 Standalone Financial Performance

Second-quarter standalone net sales rose 12% year-on-year to INR 712 crore, underscoring resilient demand in the core business despite cost headwinds. Profit after tax climbed 14% to INR 73 crore, while EBITDA grew 15%, signaling good operating leverage even as the company continued to invest in newer formats and capabilities.

Consolidated Revenue and EBITDA Growth

On a consolidated basis, Q2 revenue increased 12.2% to INR 730 crore, supported by growth across formats and channels. EBITDA jumped 15.9% to INR 198 crore and margin improved to 27.1% from 26.2%, while consolidated PAT advanced about 12% to INR 77 crore with a stable 10.6% margin, reflecting controlled costs despite some pressure below gross profit.

E-Commerce and Omni-Channel Expansion

Digital channels remained a key growth driver, with e-commerce and omni-channel sales up 12% in Q2 and contributing 14.2% of revenue. For the first half, online sales grew 11% and formed 13.6% of revenue, as Metro Brands continued to connect stores with marketplaces and leaned into emerging AI-driven discovery platforms to keep its brands visible and convenient for consumers.

Improved Gross Margin

The first half saw gross margin rise to 58.4% from 57.3% a year earlier, aided by lower average discounts on end-of-season and online sales and slightly better markups. A modestly lower contribution from e-commerce, which tends to carry higher discounting, also supported the improvement, although management cautioned that some of these gains are not fully sustainable quarter to quarter.

Festive Demand Shift Supports Q3 Opportunity

Metro Brands flagged a favorable demand shift, with a larger portion of festive buying moving into Q3 as the calendar pushed key events from September to October. Durga Puja was described as having performed very well, and other markets also showed strength on a like-for-like basis, giving management confidence in Q3 momentum as the company focuses on capturing festive footfall.

Store Network Expansion

The retailer continued to expand its footprint, opening 21 stores and closing nine in Q2 for a net addition of 12 outlets. In the first half it opened 34 stores and closed 13, taking the network to 1,053 stores at the end of September, reflecting a balance between growth and pruning underperforming locations.

Disciplined and Selective Store Expansion

Management emphasized that expansion will be selective, prioritizing profitability over hitting a headline store count. Store-opening criteria have been tightened amid high rentals and constrained real-estate supply, with H2 additions expected to exceed H1 but closures likely to remain around 2%-3%, consistent with historical levels and a focus on network quality.

Established Own Brands Remain the Core Business

Metro, Mochi and Walkway continued to anchor the portfolio, with own brands contributing about 70% of store product sales in the first half. Management argued these proprietary labels provide a strong foundation for margins and customer loyalty, complementing international partnerships and the multi-brand platform that diversify the company’s offering.

Clarks Distribution and Store Opportunity

Clarks is emerging as a key growth vector, with women’s products now present in more than 400 multi-brand outlets and a limited men’s range in over 100. The full assortment is already available on the direct-to-consumer site, and a complete exclusive-store range is slated for Q3, ahead of a planned rollout of Clarks exclusive stores once supply-chain and assortment are fully stabilized.

Positive Clarks Supply Chain and Consumer Response

Management described Clarks’ supply chain as nimble and robust, with most production localized in India and no carryover-inventory or regulatory complications. Consumer response has been “extremely high and rapid,” suggesting the brand could scale quickly once the assortment is complete, providing a meaningful incremental growth lever for Metro Brands.

Crocs Continues to Grow

Crocs remained a strong contributor, continuing to grow despite a high base built over the last few years and still accounting for less than 20% of overall business. Management noted that selective openings of Crocs-owned stores in high-heat markets may create a halo effect that benefits Metro’s sales, reinforcing the value of the partnership.

Walkway Existing-Store Productivity Improvement

Walkway, the value-focused format, is showing early signs of improvement, with like-for-like productivity gains emerging in existing stores. Metro Brands has opened more than 35 Walkway stores in the past 12-14 months on a base of around 60-70, and is now using performance data from these locations to refine its new-store formula before accelerating expansion.

Geographic Mix Remains Broadly Consistent

The company’s geographic footprint remains diversified, with roughly 31% of business from the West and 33% from the South. Management said store-to-sales contribution has stayed broadly consistent, even as metro cities have begun to slightly over-index in performance, despite a greater number of new stores opening in lower-tier markets.

Positive Medium-Term Margin Framework

Metro Brands reiterated a constructive margin outlook, expecting H2 PAT to beat H1 in line with historical seasonality and the festive demand shift. The company views a 15% PAT margin as medium- to long-term guidance, targeting a sustainable range of 13%-15% as newer businesses scale and begin contributing more meaningfully to profits.

Marketing and Capability Investment

First-half marketing spend increased to about 4% of revenue from roughly 3.25%-3.4% last year, reflecting stepped-up investment behind incubating new brands. Management expects marketing intensity to stay around 4%, while also allocating capital to talent, brand building and newer formats that are seen as crucial for long-term growth and competitive differentiation.

Planned Capital Expenditure

CapEx plans for FY 2027 and FY 2028 were pegged at around INR 80 crore-INR 100 crore annually, including store remodels to refresh the existing network. Management described roughly INR 100 crore as a reasonable level of investment to support store modernization and measured expansion without over-leveraging the balance sheet.

Frontline Compensation Changes Intended to Support Talent

To stay competitive in the retail labor market, Metro Brands plans to revise remuneration for store teams and keep pay well above minimum wage levels in most states. Front-end staff costs are expected to rise by 0.5%-1%, an increase management views as an investment in attracting and retaining talent, improving service standards and driving sales growth over time.

FILA Repositioning and Local Manufacturing

FILA is undergoing a strategic overhaul, including the start of local footwear manufacturing in India to address regulatory-related supply concerns. The repositioning focuses on sharper merchandise and pricing, with the transformation expected to unfold over the next 12-18 months before store expansion picks up from FY 2028, supported by a medium-term ambition to scale store counts significantly.

Costs Offset Part of Gross Margin Improvement

While gross margin improved, several cost lines diluted the benefit further down the income statement, including ongoing talent and brand-building investments. Higher frontline staff costs after minimum-wage revisions, modest occupancy-cost increases linked to new formats and lower treasury income versus a strong prior year all weighed on the bottom line.

Rental and Operating Cost Pressure

Management openly acknowledged rental pressure, noting that higher real-estate costs are driving negative operating leverage in some locations. Additional headwinds included front-end staff-cost inflation, continued salary investments and elevated marketing spend, all of which are deemed necessary but have short-term impact on profitability metrics.

PAT Margin Below the 15% Long-Term Target in H1

First-half PAT margin fell short of the roughly 15% level discussed with analysts, reflecting the combination of cost pressures and lower treasury gains. Management reiterated that H2 should be better than H1 and framed 15% PAT as a medium- to long-term objective, with a more realistic near-term range around 13%-15% as newer businesses mature.

Inventory Remains Elevated

Inventory levels were described as higher than desired, driven by front-loaded purchases ahead of expected raw-material cost increases and stock built for brands such as FitFlop, Clarks and Foot Locker. Management aims to normalize inventory by March, targeting around 80 working-capital days by mid to end of the next financial year and viewing about seven months of stock as the ideal level.

Store Additions Were Lower in H1

H1 saw net additions of 21 stores, with 34 openings and 13 closures, a slower pace than some investors may expect. Management attributed the moderation to tighter store-opening filters amid elevated rentals and constrained high-quality real-estate supply, but signaled that H2 additions should improve while still favoring quality over quantity.

BIS-Related Supply Uncertainty

Regulatory implementation has created supply uncertainty for selected external brands, affecting timing and readiness for formats like Foot Locker and MetroActiv. Management also highlighted higher risk for Foot Locker and FitFlop due to import dependence, noting that several growth brands still face some exposure to these rules and that expansion is being calibrated accordingly.

FILA Supply and Repositioning Challenges

FILA faced meaningful disruption, including supply interruptions, elevated old-inventory levels and the need to build new product-development capabilities for athletic footwear. These challenges forced Metro Brands to craft new product architecture, design and brand language, creating near-term drag as the company experiments and learns the right approach for the segment.

Foot Locker and MetroActiv Expansion Calibrated to Product Availability

For Foot Locker and MetroActiv, store opening plans are tightly linked to product availability, given the BIS-related supply constraints. Management stressed that capital allocation and expansion will remain aligned with supply readiness and operational progress, avoiding aggressive rollout until assortments and logistics are robust enough to support performance.

Gross-Margin Improvement Is Partly Non-Sustainable

Executives cautioned that a meaningful portion of Q2 gross-margin improvement came from lower end-of-season sale discounts, a benefit unlikely to repeat in Q3. Future margins will also vary with business mix, with formats like Walkway, Foot Locker and MetroActiv potentially exerting downward pressure as their share of sales rises due to their different pricing and discount profiles.

Raw-Material Inflation and Price Increases

The company is contending with raw-material inflation of roughly 10%-15% across its basket, prompting average selling price hikes of about 2%-4%, or slightly more on some articles. These measured increases are intended to offset cost pressures without significantly hurting demand, balancing margin protection with consumer affordability.

New-Store Productivity Still Uneven at Walkway

Walkway’s recent expansion has produced mixed results, with around 30% of new stores performing well, 30% average and 30% described as poor or failures. Management conceded that the optimal new-store formula is not yet fully established and is using this experience to refine location and assortment strategy before scaling the format more aggressively.

Sales-Per-Square-Foot Pressure from Store Openings and Cannibalization

The company noted that new stores typically operate at lower productivity than mature outlets, which weighs on average sales per square foot. Opening additional formats near successful existing stores can also create cannibalization, limiting the flow-through of same-store growth into overall sales density, a dynamic management is now factoring into its expansion plans.

Lower Treasury Income Affected PAT Growth

Other income in the first half was around INR 54 crore versus approximately INR 100 crore for the full prior year, highlighting a tougher comparison. Management said this drop in treasury gains was a significant factor behind relatively muted PAT growth, even as operating metrics like revenue and EBITDA showed healthy double-digit increases.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Strategic Outlook

Looking ahead, Metro Brands expects store closures to stay around 2%-3% and H2 to deliver stronger store additions and better PAT than H1, while aiming for a medium- to long-term PAT margin band of 13%-15%. Staff costs are projected to rise modestly, marketing to remain near 4% of revenue, CapEx around INR 100 crore annually, and inventory to normalize over the next year as transformations in Clarks and FILA steadily progress.

Metro Brands’ earnings call painted the picture of a company balancing strong core performance with cautious investment in newer brands and formats. For investors, the key takeaway is a constructive growth and margin story tempered by cost and regulatory headwinds, with management clearly focused on disciplined expansion, inventory control and building the foundations for multi-brand, omni-channel scale.

data.title: Shoppers Stop Earnings Call Signals Profitable Revival
data.description:
Shoppers Stop Limited ((IN:SHOPERSTOP)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Shoppers Stop Limited’s latest earnings call struck an upbeat note, as management highlighted a sharp turnaround in profitability and strong festive demand across key categories. While concerns linger around INTUNE’s losses, modest reported like-for-like growth and past shareholder returns, the tone was confident, with management emphasizing execution discipline, premiumization and a clearer path to debt reduction.

Strong Q2 Profitability Turnaround

On a non-GAAP basis, Q2 consolidated revenue rose 7%, while EBITDA surged 56%, underscoring operating leverage as costs stayed in check. Profit after tax flipped from a loss of INR 7 crore a year ago to a profit of INR 6 crore, and on a GAAP basis PAT improved from an INR 20 crore loss to an INR 3 crore profit.

Promotion

Healthy Consumer Demand and Festive Traction

Management reported solid consumer demand through Q2, with Raksha Bandhan and Onam performing well and the Pujo run-up in the East and Dussehra in key markets described as “significantly strong.” Stores in Pujo and Dussehra catchment areas delivered mid-teen like-for-like growth, signaling robust festive sentiment despite a challenging macro backdrop.

Accelerated Departmental Store Expansion

The company opened four departmental stores in Q2 and six in the first half, and it has raised its FY 2027 gross opening plan from 9-10 outlets to 12. Management plans six more stores by the end of September and is positioning new locations with elevated designs, modern ambience and a more premium product mix to drive higher productivity.

Departmental Store Sales and Customer Traffic

Departmental store like-for-like sales grew 2% in Q2, but management said the growth would have been 6.5% after adjusting for the festive calendar shift, with total business up 4%. Like-for-like customer entry grew 1%, while overall customer entry climbed 7.7%, suggesting network expansion and refreshed formats are drawing more shoppers into stores.

Record Loyalty Program Additions

The First Citizen loyalty program delivered its best quarter ever, adding 2.5 lakh new customers and pushing total membership to 14.1 million. The high-tier Black Card program added 19,000 members with 21,000 renewals and about a 66% renewal rate, and overall loyalty members drove 84% of sales with a repeat purchase rate of 68%.

Premiumization and Higher Basket Size

Shoppers Stop continued to shift its mix toward higher-value products, with the premium portfolio’s share rising 390 basis points to a record 73%. Average transaction value increased 9% to INR 5,471, and first-time consumers accounted for 37% of bills, indicating the brand is attracting new shoppers while nudging them toward premium categories.

Personal Shopper Program Momentum

The Personal Shopper program expanded its influence, contributing 27% of revenue, up roughly 200 basis points year-on-year. Sales through these curated services grew 13% to INR 349 crore, and management expects this high-touch, higher-ticket segment to reach about 30% of revenue by the end of the year.

Power Categories Drive Growth

Within departmental stores, key “power categories” posted strong double-digit gains, led by watches up 24% and handbags up 16% year-on-year. Fragrances grew 13%, footwear 9% and sunglasses 8%, with management also flagging very strong fashion growth heading into the festive season, underscoring a broad-based product revival.

Private Brands Profitability Improvement

The company continued pruning its private label portfolio, cutting the number of brands and reducing private-brand inventory by 26%. This rationalization helped significantly improve private-brand profitability, and the STOP × Peter England collaboration with Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands delivered encouraging early traction as a focused, co-branded play.

Beauty Business Maintains Strong Growth

The beauty segment, including Global SS Beauty, generated Q2 revenue of INR 367 crore, rising 18% year-on-year with fragrances leading at 35% growth. Estée Lauder, which had declined for four consecutive quarters, posted 4% like-for-like growth for the second straight quarter, signaling an early recovery in a key global brand partnership.

Beauty Distribution and Boutique Network Expansion

Beauty distribution revenue reached INR 168 crore, equivalent to INR 270 crore in GMV, marking a robust 59% year-on-year increase. The company also expanded its high-end boutique network to 11 stores, now comprising four Armani, three NARS, two Shiseido, one Prada and one Creed outlet, strengthening its footprint in luxury beauty.

INTUNE Operational Improvements

Value format INTUNE reported revenue of INR 72 crore and festive-adjusted like-for-like growth of 6%, with mid-teen growth during Dussehra. The repeat customer mix improved to 49% from 47% in Q1, average transaction value rose 6% and items per transaction reached 3.5, reflecting better engagement and merchandising.

INTUNE Inventory and Merchandise Freshness

INTUNE’s inventory fell by INR 33 crore year-on-year and now stands at 16 weeks of cover, highlighting a tighter supply chain. Management credited in-season clearance, improved online access, stronger full-price sell-throughs and more frequent product drops, all aimed at keeping merchandise fresher and more relevant to shoppers.

Reduced Losses in New Businesses

Newer businesses, led by INTUNE and the consolidation of ssbeauty.in into ss.com, saw EBITDA losses shrink by INR 8 crore in Q2 and INR 12 crore in H1. Management expects these losses to narrow further in the second half, pointing to better productivity and a clearer path to breakeven in adjacent formats.

Rapid E-Commerce Growth

E-commerce revenue jumped 52% year-on-year in Q2, reflecting benefits from user-interface upgrades and site integration. Average bill value online increased 9%, with watches and other power categories leading digital growth, underscoring the omnichannel potential of Shoppers Stop’s portfolio.

Inventory and Cost Discipline

Company-wide inventory was optimized by INR 78 crore year-on-year, freeing up working capital while supporting assortment freshness. Operating expenses were described as effectively flat, indicating strong cost control that preserved margins without sacrificing the in-store and online customer experience.

AI and Personalization Initiatives

Shoppers Stop expanded its data-driven toolkit, rolling out Personal Shopper app 2.0 and using shopping-behavior data to personalize store openings and merchandising. Its demand forecasting and inventory optimization system, initially deployed on private brands, was extended to INTUNE to refine stock planning and reduce markdowns.

Expansion Pipeline and Capital Allocation

Management said it has visibility to open at least 12 departmental stores annually over the next three years, subject to mall availability. Expansion across departmental stores, INTUNE and beauty distribution is expected to be funded via internal accruals, signaling confidence in cash generation and a disciplined approach to capital deployment.

Debt Reduction Strategy

The company plans to fund debt reduction through internal accruals and sustained EBITDA growth, targeting a debt-free position by Q3 FY 2027. Management noted that most large working-capital optimization steps are already done, but expects good practices in inventory and expense control to further support deleveraging.

Broad-Based Premium Demand

During Pujo and Dussehra, premium merchandise across non-apparel, fashion and apparel saw particularly strong demand, outpacing mid-segment brands. INTUNE also benefited from better merchandise availability and operating processes, suggesting both value and premium formats are finding their audience in a polarized market.

Modest Reported Like-for-Like Growth

One area of caution was departmental store like-for-like growth, which was only 2% before adjusting for the festive calendar shift. While the adjusted figure of 6.5% looks healthier and total departmental growth was 4%, investors will watch if this momentum sustains once calendar effects normalize.

INTUNE Store Portfolio Restructuring

INTUNE remains in clean-up mode, closing two high-street stores in the quarter and signaling that more loss-making locations may be exited. Management has held back on announcing the next expansion phase and asked investors to wait until Q3, emphasizing that improving the margin profile takes priority over rapid rollout.

INTUNE in Loss-Reduction Phase

Management reiterated that INTUNE’s strategy is centered on fixing margins before scaling aggressively, even as new-business losses declined 33% year-on-year on a comparable Q2 basis. The company aims to reduce these losses further in the second half, positioning the format for a more sustainable contribution in future years.

Historical Estée Lauder Weakness and Recovery

The Estée Lauder business had posted declines for four consecutive quarters before its recent stabilization, which now shows 4% like-for-like growth in each of the last two quarters. This turnaround within a key global beauty brand reduces a drag on the beauty portfolio and reinforces confidence in the segment’s growth prospects.

Investor Concerns on Past Returns

During the Q&A, one investor pointed out that retail shareholders had suffered a roughly 60%-65% negative return over the last two years. Management acknowledged the difficult phase and asked for more patience, emphasizing its focus on improving business productivity, profitability and balance-sheet health rather than chasing short-term stock performance.

Limited Scale in Owned D2C Beauty

Management noted that company-owned direct-to-consumer beauty brands currently contribute a negligible share of the overall beauty business. While the platform is benefiting from strong third-party brand growth, the in-house D2C opportunity remains largely untapped and could represent a future lever for margin expansion.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Outlook

Management upgraded its guidance for the current year to 12 departmental store openings and expects to add 10-12 stores annually over the next two to three years, with visibility of at least 12 per year for the next three. It expects the Personal Shopper program to reach about 30% of revenue by year-end, INTUNE losses to reduce in Q3 and Q4, and Q3 itself to be very strong, while maintaining mid-single-digit or slightly higher like-for-like growth and healthy profitability expansion into FY 2027.

Shoppers Stop’s earnings call painted a picture of a retailer that has regained its footing, with profitability improving, premium categories and beauty thriving and expansion backed by internal cash flow. Execution risks remain around INTUNE and sustaining like-for-like growth, but management’s sharper focus on productivity, debt reduction and customer loyalty suggests a more disciplined growth phase that investors will track closely.

data.title: Sterling and Wilson Q2 Call: Profits Return, Risks Linger
data.description:
Sterling And Wilson Renewable Energy Limited ((IN:SWSOLAR)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy’s latest earnings call struck a tone of cautious progress, as management balanced a visible turnaround in profitability and a robust order book against weaker first-half revenues and ongoing execution headwinds. Investors heard confidence around international projects, storage, and O&M growth, but also clear acknowledgement of domestic pricing pressure, supply bottlenecks, and trimmed revenue ambitions.

India’s Renewable Boom Underpins Long-Term Demand

India’s policy-driven clean energy build-out remains a powerful tailwind, with renewable and large hydro capacity now at about 308 GW, or 53% of national generation capacity. Solar has been the standout, jumping from less than 3 GW in 2014 to roughly 171 GW, and with an estimated 50 GW DC of new solar to be added in calendar 2026, slightly topping 2025’s record.

Promotion

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Government Bets Big on Green Transmission

The government’s Green Energy Corridor Phase III, with an outlay near INR 1.86 lakh crore, is designed to connect up to 135 GW of renewable energy to the grid by FY 2033. New rules mandating market-rate land compensation are expected to cut disputes and accelerate line construction, though management flagged that higher land costs could influence project economics.

Battery Storage Emerges as the Next Growth Engine

Battery storage is scaling rapidly, with 8.2 GWh added in the first half of 2026 versus less than 100 MWh a year earlier, and storage now forming nearly 40% of renewable auction capacity. The company sees 45 GWh-50 GWh commissioning in FY 2027-FY 2028 and notes regulators foresee 236 GWh by FY 2032, positioning storage as a core profit driver.

Domestic EPC and O&M Businesses Gain Scale

Domestic EPC revenue rose about 13% in the first half to INR 2,100 crores, underscoring resilient local demand despite some award delays and pricing pressure. The higher-margin O&M business grew even faster, with Q2 revenue up 55% to INR 99 crores and the half-year up 48% to INR 183 crores, as portfolio capacity climbed to 18.9 GW.

Order Book Strength Provides Multi-Year Visibility

The consolidated order book reached INR 12,481 crores at end-September, up 34% year on year and higher than March’s INR 11,813 crores, giving solid revenue visibility beyond the current fiscal. India accounts for 56% of this backlog while international projects make up 44%, giving the company a diversified geographic mix.

Margin-Focused International Order Wins

New orders totaling INR 3,626 crores in the first half were skewed almost entirely to overseas markets, where management says it is winning business at healthy levels. Four legacy projects in South Africa, Spain, and Italy have now been closed with robust margins, reinforcing the shift away from low-margin domestic bids toward more disciplined international work.

Key Wins in Rajasthan and South African Storage

In the quarter, the company secured two major contracts worth over INR 985 crores including taxes, reinforcing its solar and storage credentials. One is a 534-MW balance-of-systems project in Rajasthan for a new Indian IPP client, while the other is a 616-MW turnkey battery storage project in South Africa, the firm’s second-largest utility-scale storage deal.

Egypt’s West Minya Project Moves Into Execution

The landmark 1,000-MW AC West Minya solar project in Egypt, including 600 MWh of storage and valued around $560 million, has now received notice to proceed and begun work. Executed via 50/50 joint ventures with Hassan Allam Construction, the project is expected to contribute revenue this year, with management guiding to turnkey margins above 8%.

International Revenue Set for Second-Half Rebound

While first-half international sales were depressed, execution on the INR 5,538-crore overseas order book in Egypt and South Africa is scheduled to ramp up in the second half. Management expects a clear step-up, with Q3 stronger than Q2 and a particularly heavy revenue load in Q4 as large sites move into full swing.

Expanding Solar and Storage Bid Pipeline

The solar bid pipeline excluding storage rose to 34 GW from 27.7 GW last quarter, with 74% in India and 26% abroad, providing ample scope for fresh order inflow. Management sees bidding opportunities of about INR 45,000 crores-INR 50,000 crores across solar and storage in the second half, keeping order prospects active despite some domestic frictions.

Strategic Progress with Adani and Reliance

Under the five-year framework with the Adani Group, about 1.2 GW has already been executed and an RFQ for the next 1.2 GW has been received, with closure expected soon. The company is also closely engaged with Reliance on technical and execution planning for its integrated solar and storage hub in Kutch, with management expecting project commencement this quarter.

Floating Solar Capability Set to Open New Niche

The Tilaiya floating solar project in Jharkhand, billed as one of India’s largest for the NTPC-DVC joint venture, is now nearing completion. Management expects the know-how from this build to support upcoming floating solar tenders from central and state entities, adding another specialized segment to the company’s portfolio.

Profitability Metrics Turn the Corner

Gross profit in Q2 reached INR 140 crores, with gross margin improving to 9.2% from 8.9% a year ago and first-half margins at about 9.5%, showing better project economics. Operational EBITDA was INR 56 crores in Q2 with a 3.7% margin, slightly above last year, while recurring overheads fell roughly 11% to INR 84 crores as cost discipline kicked in.

Return to the Black After Last Year’s Hit

The company reported Q2 profit before and after tax of INR 17 crores, a sharp reversal from a loss of INR 478 crores in the same quarter last year. For the first half, profit after tax was INR 70 crores versus a loss of INR 439 crores, with management stressing that the prior-year loss was largely driven by a one-off arbitration impact.

Working Capital and Banking Lines Support Growth

The business continues to operate with negative working capital of INR 301 crores, supporting cash flow in a project-heavy model, while gross borrowings fell by INR 244 crores to INR 920 crores. Shareholders’ equity rose to INR 719 crores, and over INR 3,000 crores of fresh credit lines, including in South Africa, provide comfort for guarantees and letters of credit.

Legacy Claims and Indemnity Inflows

A settlement with a customer in Chile has been signed, and the company expects to receive around INR 156 crores under promoter indemnity in the current year. These inflows, once realized, should further bolster the balance sheet and help offset historical problem contracts that previously weighed on earnings and investor sentiment.

Scaling O&M and Global Expansion Plans

The O&M portfolio is now evenly balanced between in-house EPC builds and third-party projects, reflecting a deliberate diversification push into stable fee income. New O&M wins in Saudi Arabia and a focus on Africa, Saudi Arabia, Europe, and select Southeast Asia markets underpin management’s expectation of reaching 20 GW-25 GW by year-end and O&M revenue above INR 400 crores.

Full-Year Revenue and Margin Guidance Intact

For FY 2027, management is guiding to up to 10% revenue growth, excluding potential Reliance orders, with Q3 seen as an improvement and Q4 as the strongest quarter. It expects EPC gross margins of 8%-10%, O&M gross margins near 20%, operational EBITDA margins of at least 4%-4.5%, and an order book above INR 10,000 crores at fiscal year-end.

First-Half Revenue Under Pressure

Despite strategic progress, Q2 revenue slipped to INR 1,527 crores from INR 1,749 crores a year earlier, and was also down slightly from Q1’s INR 1,590 crores. First-half revenue declined about 11% year on year to INR 3,118 crores, underscoring the lag between order wins and actual execution on the ground.

Sharp Drop in International Revenue Pre-Ramp

International revenue in the first half plunged to INR 165 crores from INR 929 crores, mainly because four major projects in South Africa, Spain, and Italy reached completion while new ones had yet to start. Management framed this as a timing issue rather than a demand problem, expecting the second half to see a strong recovery as fresh sites mobilize.

Delayed Starts and NTPs Slow Execution

Eight projects, split evenly between India and overseas, had not yet begun due to delays in notices to proceed, PPAs, and financing arrangements, particularly for three PSU projects and several IPP contracts. The company expects most of the Indian projects to move in the next one to two months, with meaningful revenue from PSU work now pushed into Q4.

Domestic Solar Cell Bottlenecks Inflate Costs

New ALMM II rules requiring use of modules made with Indian cells have exposed a mismatch between more than 200 GW of module capacity and only about 35 GW of cell capacity, driving up compliant module prices by 15%-17%. Many developers are recalibrating project economics and tariffs, causing them to delay EPC awards and further slowing the domestic execution pipeline.

PPA, Grid, and Curtailment Risks Weigh on Pace

Roughly 40 GW-50 GW of awarded renewable capacity is still awaiting signed PPAs, creating uncertainty and pushing out project timelines for EPC players. At the same time, grid constraints have led to curtailment of solar generation in Rajasthan and parts of western India, delaying projects in Rajasthan and Gujarat by several quarters.

Competitive Intensity Squeezes Domestic Margins

Reverse auctions and low entry barriers have encouraged aggressive bidding from newer players at prices that management believes are hard to sustain, compressing industry margins. Sterling and Wilson has deliberately walked away from some domestic tenders below its cost appetite, leading to fewer local wins but protecting profitability as it leans on international markets.

Battery Costs and Warranty Risk Complicate Bids

After years of decline, battery prices rose in 2026, even as customers demand longer performance warranties that transfer more risk onto EPC contractors. Management also highlighted that some battery and hybrid projects in the market have been annulled or terminated because their bid prices proved unworkable, reinforcing the need for disciplined pricing.

Operating EBITDA Hit by Lower International Mix

Integration and Platform Synergies

The Housing.com platform is being woven into Aurum’s developer, broker, transaction, financing, and living businesses to boost lead quality and conversion. Cost Cuts and Path to Housing Profitability

Within a week of closing the deal, Aurum implemented roughly INR 120 crore of cost reductions at Housing.com without notable revenue impact. The focus now shifts to growth, with another INR 100–150 crore of revenue targeted over four to six quarters and a stated goal to move Housing into profitability within 12–18 months.

Rental Segment Turns the Corner

Rental Metrics and Capacity Build-Out

Residential rentals managed 8,900 signed units and collected INR 35 crore of rent in the quarter, with AI-enabled bookings rising 7.6 times sequentially. Management said rental consolidation is largely complete, the segment is now profitable, and it plans to increase beds across HelloWorld and NestAway while targeting 88% occupancy by year-end.

Capital and Mortgage Business Scales Up

The capital segment, though still small, grew revenue to INR 4.3 crore from INR 1.2 crore a year ago and delivered INR 0.4 crore in profit. KuberX disbursed INR 200 crore of loans in September alone, implying a current run rate of INR 2,400 crore and pointing to a much larger mortgage opportunity ahead.

Healthy Cash Generation and Near-Zero Debt

Operating cash flow from continuing operations in the first half rose to INR 60.8 crore, comfortably covering capital expenditure of INR 8.8 crore and lease obligations. The company ended the quarter with INR 191.6 crore in cash and investments and less than INR 1 crore in bank and other borrowings, leaving it effectively debt-free.

Balance Sheet Strengthened by Equity Infusion

Total assets jumped to INR 1,641 crore from INR 948 crore in March, while shareholders’ equity nearly doubled to INR 1,020 crore, primarily due to the Housing.com consolidation. The promoter further committed capital through convertible warrants, paying 25% upfront, with the balance due upon exercise within 18 months.

AI Investments Aim at Productivity Gains

Management reported that business value generated per team member has already risen from about INR 40 lakh to over INR 50 lakh, with a year-end target of INR 56 lakh. The company is investing in AI to stitch together a unified journey from property discovery through financing and living, though benefits are still in early stages.

Expanding Market Coverage

Aurum currently partners with roughly 18,000–19,000 channel partners and more than 1,300 developers, but sees headroom to more than double both. Housing.com’s sizeable base of monthly active users and tens of millions of app downloads further broadens the funnel for the group’s transaction and rental offerings.

Leveraging Rentals and Education Payments

Management is exploring the relaunch of Housing.com’s rental and education payments services in combination with NestAway’s existing operations. With NestAway already processing about INR 35 crore of rentals each quarter, the company sees a clear opportunity to layer payments and ancillary services onto this flow.

Tax Assets and Carry-Forward Losses

The acquisition of Housing.com brings with it INR 1,020 crore of carry-forward losses that could provide meaningful tax shields over time. Aurum is seeking expert opinions on how best to utilize these losses across the group structure to optimize its overall tax position.

Pre-Profit Status and Deep Cost Cuts at Housing

Management reiterated that Housing.com remains pre-profit despite the substantial cost reset and that the heavier lifting ahead will be on the revenue side. The recent INR 120 crore cost reduction was described as a deep, one-time exercise, with further margin gains expected to flow primarily from scale and monetization.

Rationalization in Rental Units and Beds

NestAway has seen a planned reduction in units as the company consolidated properties across pin codes to sharpen unit-level profitability. HelloWorld also shed non-profitable buildings in the first quarter, creating a cleaner base from which to ramp up occupancy and yields.

Rising Other Expenses and Tax Rate

Other expenses rose to INR 62.2 crore or 47.8% of revenue, up from 45% in Q1, largely because the fast-growing distribution business carries higher variable costs. The effective tax rate was around 37%, as profitable entities currently pay tax while losses in some subsidiaries are not yet recognized as deferred tax assets.

One-Off Gain Skews H1 Profit

Headline H1 net profit of INR 49.5 crore included INR 45.5 crore from discontinued operations tied to the sale of a Navi Mumbai building. Excluding this one-time gain, profit after tax from continuing operations was INR 3.9 crore, a marked improvement on the INR 17.9 crore loss recorded in the first half of the prior year.

Early-Stage Capital Segment and Working-Capital Mix

Despite high growth rates, the capital segment still contributed only a fraction of group revenue compared with distribution and rentals. Current liabilities slightly exceeded current assets, but management noted that a sizable portion reflects lease liabilities, which are backed by corresponding right-of-use assets on the balance sheet.

Management Focused on Integration Over Deals

With the Housing.com acquisition now closed, management stressed that its immediate priority is integration and moving the platform to profitability. As a result, Aurum does not plan to actively chase new acquisitions in the near term, though it remains open to compelling strategic opportunities if they arise.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Growth Ambitions

Looking ahead, management aims to make Housing.com profitable in 12–18 months, with internal break-even targeted within four to six quarters and revenue scaling by INR 100–150 crore over that period. The company expects revenue per team member to rise steadily for the next several quarters, aims to lift rental occupancy to about 88%, sharply ramp up KuberX home-loan disbursements, and expand its network of channel partners and developers as integration synergies start to show.

Aurum PropTech’s earnings call painted a picture of a platform at an inflection point, balancing disciplined execution with aggressive scaling. While integration risk, tax complexity, and pre-profit assets remain watch points, the combination of strong growth, improving profitability, and a fortified balance sheet keeps investor sentiment firmly constructive around the stock’s medium-term trajectory.

Newer-Vintage Loan Portfolio Expands Rapidly

The company invested $703 million in the quarter, including seven new balance sheet loans totaling $222 million, and has originated $1.4 billion of loans year to date. The loan portfolio has grown more than 50% over the last 12 months, with about 90% of loans and nearly all multifamily exposure originated since late 2024, reducing legacy risk.

Selective Capital Deployment Lifts Earning Assets

After factoring in payoffs, sales, and amortization, Ladder’s combined loan and securities books expanded by roughly $570 million. Balance sheet loans now account for about half of total assets, and management aims to steadily raise that share while staying nimble if lending volumes soften.

High-Quality, Floating-Rate Securities Book

Ladder added $481 million of mostly AAA-rated securities during the quarter and continued buying into October, pushing the securities portfolio to $2.3 billion, or 37% of assets. The book offers a 5.5% weighted average yield, 99% investment-grade exposure, 97% AAA concentration, 96% floating-rate assets, and about three years of duration.

Structurally Positioned for Higher Rates

At quarter end, 92% of the company’s $4.8 billion of interest-earning assets were floating rate, while 57% of its funding was fixed rate with a 5.3% average coupon. Management estimates every 25-basis-point increase in SOFR adds about $0.01 per share per quarter to distributable earnings, reinforcing its higher-rate upside.

Robust Liquidity and Conservative Leverage

Adjusted leverage stood at 2.5x, while liquidity reached $784 million including same-day revolver capacity, supporting flexibility in a choppy market. The company also held $1.2 billion of mostly AAA securities unencumbered, with unsecured debt at 69% of total and an unencumbered pool covering 73% of assets, largely in first mortgages and high-grade paper.

Share Repurchases at Deep Discount to Book

Ladder bought back $8.2 million of stock in the quarter, or 871,000 shares, at an average price of $9.38, roughly a 31% discount to undepreciated book. Year to date, repurchases total $29.6 million across three million shares, and $83.8 million remains under the program, though buybacks are constrained by the need to reassure bondholders.

Dividend Backed by Asset-Liability Alignment

The company paid a $0.23 per share dividend for the quarter and emphasized its durability under current conditions. Management pointed to the predominantly floating-rate asset base, fixed-rate funding, and ongoing loan growth as the core engines supporting steady dividend coverage.

Real Estate Platform Provides Stable Income and Gains

Ladder’s $900 million real estate segment produced steady net operating income, anchored by 148 net lease assets mostly backed by investment-grade tenants with 6.4 years of remaining term. Over 13 years, the firm has generated $250 million of profits from 69 sales, including $76 million of gains since the pandemic, underscoring long-term value creation.

Office Exposure Winding Down Without Major Losses

Of the five largest office exposures flagged in 2022, four have now paid off, including the Jacksonville campus, and none have produced losses to date. The remaining loan in that group is expected to repay in full before year-end, easing concerns around concentrated office risk.

Multifamily Book Skews to Safer Vintages

Management said it does not foresee meaningful stress in its multifamily portfolio because it largely avoided the frothiest 2021–2022 vintages. Only one legacy multifamily loan remains, with a $10.2 million balance, and the company does not anticipate an impairment on that asset.

Credit Reserves Viewed as Sufficient

The CECL reserve stood at $44 million, or $0.35 per share, representing 1.48% of the loan portfolio at quarter end. Management argued this level reflects the newer-vintage book and current market risks and said it believes reserves are adequate, though it acknowledged they could grow if the portfolio expands.

Hunting for Real Estate and Distressed Opportunities

Ladder is actively seeking to buy more real estate equity, especially newer assets in lease-up where it sees strong upside. Management also flagged interest in M&A, acquiring assets from liquidity-constrained sellers, and playing across the capital stack as owner, partner, mezzanine lender, or buyer of platforms.

Management’s Capital at Risk with Shareholders

Executives and directors collectively own about 13% of the company, making them its largest shareholder bloc. They reiterated priorities of protecting principal, growing earnings, and compounding long-term value, stressing alignment between management and investors.

Leveraging a Higher-for-Longer Backdrop

Management expects diverse earnings streams from loans, securities, and real estate to fuel a strong fourth quarter. They believe Ladder is well positioned to benefit from a higher-rate environment and plan to deploy remaining capital into high-rate opportunities to enhance earnings in coming quarters.

Higher Rates Weigh on Refinancing and Originations

The sharp global rise in interest rates is curbing refinancing activity and throttling the loan origination pipeline. Management said deals have been pulled, contracts abandoned, and borrowers are pushing for lower prices as financing costs bite, dampening near-term transaction flow.

Loan Demand Not Yet Absorbing Securities Capital

Demand for high-quality loan originations is currently too soft to absorb all capital freed from securities, according to management. The acquisition pipeline has largely evaporated as funding costs jumped, forcing Ladder to remain patient and selective rather than chase weaker credits.

Nonaccrual Loans and Minneapolis Takeover Plan

As of September 30, Ladder had two nonaccrual loans totaling $61 million, including a $51 million Los Angeles hotel position and an office loan in Minneapolis. The company expects to assume ownership of the Minneapolis property in the fourth quarter, positioning it to manage or reposition the asset directly.

Minneapolis Charge-Off and Legacy CMBS Loss

Ladder charged off $3.5 million of existing CECL allowance tied to the Minneapolis office loan, cutting its carrying value to $9.9 million, or about $67 per square foot. It also recorded a $4.5 million distributable loss on a legacy fixed-rate CMBS position, though this had already been reflected in book value via other comprehensive income.

Carmel Retail Disposal to Realize Modest Loss

A previously foreclosed retail property in Carmel, New York, is under contract for sale and expected to produce a roughly $600,000 loss, which was taken this quarter. Management framed the impact as modest and part of an ongoing clean-up of smaller legacy problem assets.

Multifamily Rent Pressures Emerging

Executives noted that multifamily rents are falling in most markets, with exceptions such as New York and San Francisco holding up better. Lower-rent properties catering to lower-income tenants are seeing more pressure, though Ladder believes its selective exposure reduces direct risk from this trend.

Management reiterated its plan to grow the loan portfolio, deploy capital where risk-adjusted returns are most attractive, and harvest gains across businesses to drive earnings and support the dividend. The bank sold $543 million of single-family residential loans in the quarter, generating a $16.4 million gain, and agreed to sell $429 million of multifamily loans in fiscal 2027’s first quarter, with an anticipated $7 million gain. These transactions lifted non-interest income to $38.1 million from $24.2 million but also reduced loans receivable by $977 million, driving the loan-to-deposit ratio down to 89.3% and trimming future purchase-accounting accretion by roughly $0.5 million per quarter.

Deposits increased by $389 million in the quarter, with non-interest-bearing balances up 1.5%, interest-bearing up 0.9% and time deposits up 3.2%, pushing core deposits to 81.8% of total versus 80.6% in June and 77.9% a year earlier. Capital, Liquidity and Net Interest Margin Outlook

Washington Federal underscored its strong capital and liquidity, pointing to CET1 of 11.4%, total risk-based capital of 14.4% and $4.2 billion of on-balance-sheet liquidity backed by substantial borrowing capacity. Still, management stressed that these levels remain elevated versus history, in part due to a large $54 million C&I relationship with a private-equity-owned manufacturer that produced an unusually high loss, lifting the fiscal 2026 loss rate to 22 basis points including the impairment.

Resolution of Problem Credits and Allowance Position

The troubled $54 million C&I relationship was resolved during the quarter, contributing to reduced criticized and non-performing assets, and executives said a remaining sizable real estate credit of about $40 million is expected to be sold without a similarly significant loss. The allowance for credit losses, including unfunded commitments, covered 1.04% of gross loans overall and 1.37% of commercial loans, up from 1.3% a year earlier, reflecting continued caution amid external headwinds.

Macro Headwinds and Elevated Expense Base

Looking ahead, management expects net interest margin to expand modestly over the next quarter or two if interest rates hold steady, with earning assets remaining relatively flat to modestly higher as loan growth offsets sales. They plan to defend net interest income, see expenses around $115 million and “a little bit flat” next quarter, assume roughly 50% deposit betas in a scenario with one or two additional rate hikes, and expect credit loss rates to revert toward historical norms, while the multifamily loan sale is slated to close in December with an estimated $7 million gain and the EverBank transaction still on track for early 2027.

In sum, Washington Federal’s earnings call balanced strong full-year performance, healthy pipelines and ample capital and liquidity against near-term earnings volatility, elevated though improving credit metrics and investor skepticism around the EverBank deal. Management’s message to markets was clear: core operations remain sound, the merger is central to long-term growth and efficiency gains, and they see the current challenges as manageable rather than structural.

Landmark AUM Milestone and Growth Momentum

Stage 1 assets improved marginally to 99.40%, Stage 2 assets eased to 31 basis points, and Stage 3 provisioning coverage stood high at 59.8%, giving comfort on future credit losses.

Credit Costs Moderate Further

Credit costs continued to trend lower, with Q2 FY 2027 credit cost at 10 basis points versus 16 basis points in the prior-year quarter. For H1 FY 2027, credit cost was only 8 basis points, reflecting benign delinquencies and strong collection performance.

Diversified Product Growth Across Segments

Growth was broad-based, as Home Loan AUM growth improved to 22% from 20% in the prior quarter, indicating acceleration in the flagship product. Lease rental discounting grew 39% year-over-year, loan against property 26%, and Developer Finance 13%, keeping the AUM mix diversified with Home Loans at 53.9% of the book.

With an average ticket size of INR 28 lakh, the segment is increasingly prime, as customers with bureau scores above 750 rose to 65% and salaried borrowers formed 66% of the base.

Sambhav Expansion Strategy Gains Traction

Management said Sambhav is progressing well across B2C, B2B and B2C sourcing channels, underscoring a multi-pronged approach to scale. The company aims to reach or exceed a INR 600 crore monthly disbursal run rate by year-end and gradually lift Sambhav to around 20% of the Home Loan mix next year and 30% over the next three to four years.

Lower Cost of Funds and Better Gross Spread

Cost of funds declined 17 basis points sequentially from 7.2% in Q1 to about 7% in Q2, mainly driven by converting fixed-rate liabilities into floating-rate instruments. Gross spread improved 7 basis points to 1.8%, helping offset a 10-basis-point reduction in portfolio yield and supporting overall profitability.

Diversified Borrowing Profile Supports Stability

The borrowing mix remained diversified, with money market instruments at 56%, bank lines at 35% and NHB funding at 9%. Within this, NCDs rose to 50.8%, up 430 basis points sequentially, partially replacing bank borrowing, commercial paper and NHB, and strengthening market-based funding.

Healthy Capital and Regulatory Buffers

Capital adequacy stood at a comfortable 21.24%, providing room to support growth without immediate capital needs. The principal business criterion was 60.49% and individual Home Loan criterion 50.6%, both above regulatory thresholds, confirming compliance with key sector norms.

Expanded Branch Network Underpins Growth

The operating network expanded to 223 branches across 182 locations, enhancing physical reach into newer geographies. This footprint supports both prime and near-prime expansion and underlies the strong disbursement and AUM growth trends reported.

Higher Fee Income from Cross-Sell

Fee and commission income rose, helped by higher insurance income and increased foreclosure fees. Management linked the insurance uptick to stronger Sambhav disbursements and better attachment rates, confirming that cross-sell remains an important earnings lever.

Continued Investment in Near-Prime and New Markets

Management emphasized sustained investment in Sambhav and the non-top-six market structure to build long-term franchises. The company plans to continue investing heavily in near-prime segments, top-six-plus markets this year, and affordable housing in the next year, even at the cost of higher near-term expenses.

Floating-Rate Balance Sheet Shapes Rate Sensitivity

Around 88% of assets and liabilities are on floating rates, creating a largely matched interest-rate profile. Management expects about 80% to 82% of future repo hikes to flow through to cost of funds, with similar pass-through to portfolio yields, limiting structural margin risk but heightening short-term volatility.

Developer Finance Growth Commitment

Although the Developer Finance portfolio declined sequentially due to higher project-led repayments and slower disbursements, management stressed this was not a strategic pullback. Sanctions rose sharply in the first half, and the company targets Developer Finance growth of around 15% to 17% of the portfolio over time.

Assignment Strategy Within Defined Corridor

The company assigned about INR 1,428 crore of loans in the quarter versus INR 2,600 crore in the previous quarter, indicating tactical moderation. Management reiterated that assignments will generally stay within an 11% to 13% corridor of the book, guided by principal business criteria and asset-liability management considerations.

Sequential NIM and Yield Moderation

Net interest margin moderated by 10 basis points sequentially to 3.7%, reflecting lower portfolio yields and changing funding dynamics. Portfolio yield dipped from 8.9% in Q1 to 8.8% in Q2, a modest decline that management is watching amid a shifting rate environment.

Developer Finance Portfolio Movement

The Developer Finance portfolio’s sequential decline was driven by higher repayments and slower disbursements rather than asset-quality weakness. Management noted that, despite the quarter-on-quarter drop, the business still grew 13% year-over-year, supporting its medium-term growth intentions.

Marginal Uptick in Home Loan GNPA

Home Loan GNPA increased slightly to 36 basis points from 34 basis points in the previous quarter, while Home Loan NNPA rose by 1 basis point to 16 basis points. Management described this as a modest deterioration within an otherwise strong Home Loan asset-quality profile.

Isolated LRD Account Migration to NPA

LRD GNPA came in at 2 basis points following the movement of a single retail LRD account from Stage 2 to Stage 3. Excluding this one account, management said the LRD portfolio remains strong, indicating no broad-based stress in the segment.

Potential Impact from Insurance Commission Rules

Management cautioned that final insurance commission guidelines, if similar to the draft, could impact income from cross-sell. With roughly 10% to 11% of PBT coming from cross-sell and only 4% to 5% likely offset, the company anticipates a possible 6% to 7% hit to PBT and sees opex-to-NTI potentially flat next year under that scenario.

Rising Salary Expenses Reflect Growth Investments

Salary expenses increased 19% year-over-year in the quarter, driven by higher headcount, senior leadership hires and continued investment in Sambhav and other businesses. Management expects salary costs to keep rising year-over-year for the next four quarters before stabilizing, highlighting a deliberate build-out phase.

Prime-Market Pricing and Attrition Risk

Management flagged that higher repo rates could lift cost of funds, with uncertainty around whether banks will raise new acquisition pricing accordingly. If pricing does not keep pace, the company could face higher attrition, particularly in prime housing and some LRD loans, pressuring both growth and margins.

Guidance Held Amid Rate Uncertainty

The company did not revise guidance, noting that the full impact of the recent rate hike on acquisition pricing and balance transfers is still unclear. It indicated AUM growth could ease from 25% toward 22% to 23% if attrition increases, while margin pressure could add 1 to 2 basis points if acquisition pricing lags funding costs.

Expected Cost of Funds Trend Higher

Management called the roughly 7% September exit cost of funds a starting point for an upward trajectory as rates rise. In a scenario of three 25-basis-point repo hikes, it estimated that around 60 to 61 basis points could flow through to cost of funds by the exit period, underscoring the importance of pricing discipline.

Lower Income from De-Recognized Loans

Income from de-recognized loans fell to about INR 40 crore in the quarter from roughly INR 68 crore previously, mainly due to lower assignment volume. Assignments declined to around INR 1,428 crore versus INR 2,600 crore, trimming this ancillary income stream.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Strategic Priorities

Management reaffirmed yearly AUM growth guidance of 21% to 23% and ROA of 2.1% to 2.3%, while flagging around 25 basis points of NIM compression for the year, with a further one or two basis points possible if pricing pressure persists. It expects Developer Finance to grow at 15% to 17% of the portfolio, Sambhav to hit a INR 600 crore monthly disbursal run rate by year-end and reach around 20% of the Home Loan mix next year and 30% over three to four years, while assignments remain at 11% to 13% of the book and opex-to-NTI is reduced by 1% each year.

The earnings call painted a picture of a lender that is scaling rapidly, protecting asset quality and investing for the future, even as it prepares for a tougher rate and regulatory backdrop. For investors, Bajaj Housing Finance’s blend of strong growth, tight credit costs and clear strategic focus on Sambhav and diversified products suggests a resilient franchise, though near-term margins and fee income bear watching as rates and rules evolve.
